description: Blargg-framework NES test: dummy-read side effects of $2000-$3FFF-mirrored PPU register reads during indexed/absolute addressing. No source patch: proves build.py's clone-at-SHA + build + manifest path end-to-end on a suite that needs none.
license: public domain / freely redistributable (Shay Green's test framework + Joel Yliluoma's test); see upstream cpu_dummy_reads/source/readme.txt
golden_gate_reason: The unmodified source needs ca65 '--feature force_range' to assemble at all (the shared common/delay.s idiom 'adc #-1' is rejected by every available ca65, including HEAD -- see PROVENANCE.md); once it assembles, the rebuilt ROM is the same length as upstream's shipped binary but ~184 bytes differ (offsets from 0x6027 into the CHARS-adjacent PRG bank onward), most consistent with cc65's longbranch macro (jeq/jne/jpl/jmi in common/shell.inc's use of asminc/longbranch.mac) picking a different short/long branch encoding than whatever built the shipped ROM. Verified behaviourally instead, same exception the plan already grants the NES 2005-era asm6f sources (section 1, decision #9's note; section 5's build.py description).

commands: ca65 --feature force_range --smart -t nes -I common -I /opt/rom-toolchain/cc65-asminc -o cpu_dummy_reads.o cpu_dummy_reads.s
